subtopics.title: Monopoly — One Seller, and the Price Maker's Diagram

questions.question: A monopoly is defined as:
options: A single seller of a product with no close substitutes, protected by blocked entry
Any large company listed on the JSE
A market with a few interdependent sellers

questions.question: Selling 10 units at R20, or 11 units at R19: the marginal revenue of the eleventh unit is:
options: R9 — the R19 it brings in minus the R1 discount now given on each of the other 10 units

questions.question: Having found output where MR equals MC, the monopolist's PRICE is read:
options: Off the MR curve at that output
Off the demand curve, straight up from that quantity

questions.question: Monopoly profit can persist into the long run because:
options: Monopolists have lower costs than all rivals
Entry is blocked, so no newcomers arrive to compete the profit away

subtopics.title: Oligopoly — the Few, the Kink, and the Cartel Temptation

questions.question: The defining feature of oligopoly is:
options: Mutual interdependence — each firm's best move depends on rivals' responses

questions.question: On the kinked demand curve, the segment ABOVE the kink is elastic because:
options: If one firm raises its price, rivals do not follow and its customers desert
Demand is always elastic for fuel

questions.question: Because price wars are mutually destructive, oligopolists compete mainly through:
options: Non-price weapons — branding, advertising, loyalty programmes, features, service and sponsorships

questions.question: Cartels are described as inherently unstable because:
options: Their prices are too low to sustain
Each member profits by secretly shading price below the agreement to steal volume

subtopics.title: Monopolistic Competition — Many Sellers, Each Slightly Special

questions.question: Monopolistic competition combines:
options: Many sellers and free entry with differentiated products that give each seller slight price power

questions.question: The firm's demand curve in monopolistic competition is:
options: Gently downward-sloping — flatter than a monopolist's, because close substitutes wait next door

questions.question: Long-run equilibrium is reached when entry shifts each firm's demand curve leftward until it:
options: Just touches the average cost curve — tangency, price equal to AC, normal profit only

questions.question: EXCESS CAPACITY in monopolistic competition means:
options: Firms produce more than the market demands
The tangency lands on the falling part of AC, so each firm produces less than the cost-minimising output — the permanently half-empty restaurant

subtopics.title: The Four Structures Side by Side

questions.question: Across the four structures, ENTRY is respectively:
options: Free (perfect competition), free (monopolistic competition), difficult (oligopoly), blocked (monopoly)

questions.question: Long-run economic profit is possible only under:
options: Oligopoly and monopoly — because entry is difficult or blocked

questions.question: The famous qualification to monopoly's poor efficiency verdict is that:
options: Monopoly output exceeds the competitive level
Where scale is genuinely natural one producer is cheapest — regulation, not break-up, is the remedy — and protected profits can fund large-scale research

questions.question: The "two dials" that generate all four market structures are:
options: The slope of the demand curve the firm faces and the ease of entry

questions.question: The bridge company differs from the tomato seller because:
options: It has no next table for buyers to step to — it chooses its price rather than accepting one

questions.question: When the bridge cuts its toll from R20 to R19 to attract one more crosser, the true gain is less than R19 because:
options: The extra crosser might swim anyway
Everyone now pays R19 — the discount to all existing crossers eats into the new revenue, which is why MR sits below price

questions.question: Even a monopolist's toll has a ceiling because:
options: The Competition Act caps all prices
At a high enough toll people swim, cycle the long way or stay home — the demand curve is its constraint
Banks refuse to finance high tolls

questions.question: One bridge carrying everyone at lower cost than two half-empty ones illustrates:
options: Natural monopoly — where the sensible remedy is a regulator at the tollgate, not a rival bridge

subtopics.title: Three Petrol Stations and a Staring Contest

questions.question: Station A will not RAISE its price ten cents because:
options: B and C keep theirs and A's regulars drift down the road, leaving A alone with empty pumps
B and C would raise theirs higher

questions.question: Station A will not CUT its price ten cents because:
options: B and C must match within the hour, leaving all three selling to the same customers at lower revenue
Its pumps cannot handle more volume

questions.question: The months-long frozen price with no agreement is the real-life version of:
options: The kinked demand curve — up loses alone, down gains nothing, so the price sticks

questions.question: The rainy-evening handshake to raise all three prices from Monday is:
options: Tacit price leadership, which is always legal
Overt collusion — a cartel, illegal in South Africa and undermined anyway by each member's temptation to cheat

questions.question: Each salon is "a tiny bridge" because:
options: Her loyal customers will pay somewhat more before walking, giving her slight price power over her own variant

questions.question: When salon three's margins fatten, the predictable consequence is:
options: New salons open on the street, slice away customers, and the fattening stops at normal profit

questions.question: The empty chairs on eleven half-busy salons represent:
options: Excess capacity — the cost of a street where everyone is slightly different, paid for with the benefit of variety

questions.question: Matching the town's businesses to structures: tomato tables, the bridge, the petrol stations and the salons are respectively:
options: Oligopoly, monopolistic competition, monopoly, perfect competition
Monopoly, oligopoly, perfect competition, monopolistic competition
Monopolistic competition, perfect competition, monopoly, oligopoly
Perfect competition, monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic competition
